---
title: "source and restore-repo"
---

`proj source` fetches raw inputs from the remotes that supply them, outside a
build. `proj restore-repo` clones a GitHub repository and then fetches its raw
inputs. Both follow projr 0.9 (`projr_source()`, `projr_restore_repo()`,
SATVILab/projr@5f915ef `R/source.R`, `R/restore-repo.R`, with 6acb9b8's
`remote`). Production builds run the same fetch for `build.source` before their
start hooks; see [Raw-input sources](../configuration.qmd#raw-input-sources).

## proj source

```bash
proj source                                   # build.source, or each label's publisher
proj source --label raw-survey --remote github:survey-team --version 0.6
proj source --version 1.2.3                   # an exact build
proj source --version current                 # the inputs this checkout's build used
proj source --conflict remote                 # replace local changes without asking
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--label` | each source's selection | Labels to fetch (repeat or comma-separate). |
| `--remote` | `build.source`, else discovery | A registered remote: its title, or `local:<title>`/`github:<title>` when both types use it. |
| `--version` | the configured `version`, else `latest` | `latest`, `x`, `x.y`, `x.y.z`, or `current`. |
| `--cue` | `if-change` | `if-change`, `always`, `if-empty` or `never`. |
| `--strategy` | configured | `sync-diff`, `sync-purge`, `download-all` or `download-missing`. |
| `--inspect` | configured | `manifest`, `file` or `none`. |
| `--conflict` | ask on a terminal, else configured | `error`, `local` (keep changed local files) or `remote` (replace them). |
| `--profile` | the projr profile order | Profiles for the project's configuration. |

Which remotes are used:

- With `--remote`, that remote, with its `build.source` settings when it is
  listed there and its `get` settings otherwise. `--label` replaces its content.
- Otherwise the remotes under `build.source`; `--label` narrows them, and a label
  none of them supplies is an error ("Name a remote").
- Without `build.source`, each label comes from the one registered ordinary
  remote (local or GitHub) that has published it at its latest version. A label
  published by two remotes needs `--remote`. A remote that has not published a
  manifest (a missing Release or archive folder) is skipped; a remote that cannot
  be listed or read is an error (decision D5; projr treats it as unpublished).

Arguments override the configured settings for this call. Every selected label is
checked before anything changes: the remote's metadata is read, the label's
newest build at or before the selected version is chosen, and the files needed
are downloaded into private staging and checked against that build's MD5s.

Local changes: `.projr/source/<label>.json` records the files of the last fetch
(projr's Git-ignored record). A file the fetch would overwrite or delete that
differs from the record, or that the record does not list, is a local change.
On a terminal, `proj source` lists them and asks whether to keep or replace
them, or cancel; otherwise `--conflict` or the configured policy decides, and
`error` stops with the list:

```text
raw-data (local:archive): local changes would be overwritten or deleted: data.csv.
Run proj source to choose, or set conflict: local to keep these files or conflict: remote to replace them.
```

`--non-interactive` and `--machine` never ask. Changed labels are staged beside
their directories (a copy of the current files with the planned changes,
checked) and then replaced together; a directory that changes during the fetch
stops it before anything is replaced. `--version current` delegates to
[`proj restore`](get.qmd): `--conflict remote` maps to `--clear`, `local` is an
error, and `--remote` names the destination (a local remote too, as with
`proj restore --destination local:<title>`).

`proj source` holds the project's build claim (`.projr/build.lock`), so it cannot
run during a build or alongside a restore. The result lists each label:

```json
{"labels": [{"label": "raw-data", "remote": "local:archive", "version": "v1.2.4",
  "status": "update", "written": 2, "removed": 0, "kept": 0}]}
```

`status` is `present` (left alone under `if-empty`), `pinned` (the exact pinned
build is already in place), `current` or `update`. With `--machine` the result is
under `result.source`.

## proj restore-repo

```bash
proj restore-repo owner/analysis              # clone into ./analysis, fetch every raw label
proj restore-repo owner/analysis copy --label raw-data --remote github:archive
proj restore-repo analysis                    # a repository of the token's user
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `repo` | `owner/repo`, or `repo` for one owned by the user of `GITHUB_PAT`, `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`. |
| `path` | Directory to clone into; default: the repository name. |
| `--label` | Labels to fetch. |
| `--remote` | A registered remote, as for `proj source`. |

The clone uses the installed `git` and its own credential configuration, from
`<GITHUB_SERVER_URL>/<owner>/<repo>.git` (default `https://github.com`). With
`--non-interactive`, Git is told not to prompt for credentials. In the clone,
`proj source` then runs with `cue: always` and `conflict: error`. A failure exits
non-zero with the reason (projr returns `FALSE`); a completed clone stays in
place. With `--machine` the result is under `result.restore_repo`.
